newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania facing crucial 24 hours, says Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albania facing crucial 24 hours, says Italy.

text.p: Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said on Tuesday that the next 24 hours could be crucial for Albania and called on all political groups to overcome arrogance and make mutual concessions.
"The next 24 hours are very important for the future of Albania," he told reporters after addressing a parliamentary commission.
Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino warned earlier that deadlock over planned elections had pushed the country to the brink of a "deeper crisis with unforseen consequences".

Andreatta called on all sides "to overcome arrogance and diffidence and to seek together, notwithstanding the splits that have occurred, to legitimise the electoral process with reciprocal concessions".

Italian news agencies quoted Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who is on a visit to Budapest, as saying international mediator Franz Vranitzky had urged the parties to talk until midnight to try to unblock the situation.
Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, has repeatedly travelled to Tirana to try to broker a deal on elections scheduled for June 29.

Albanian President Sali Berisha has pushed an electoral law through parliament which has been contested by Fino's Socialist Party and other forces in the nine-party Government of National Reconciliation. Most are threatening to boycott the election.
